va_hive_boulder.blurb: A single large, rounded boulder perched on a low platform of blocks, along the Listening Rock trail in Grayson Highlands State Park. It is one of the busier boulders on that trail and carries about eleven problems. Expect a friendly spread, from VB and V0 warm-ups through the middle grades up to a few problems around V4 and V5, with the best-known lines in the V0 to V4 range. Holds are mostly crimps and jugs with some slopers, landings are generally flat and reliable, and the top-outs run from medium to tall, so bring more than one pad. Reaching it is a short, uneven stroll along the trail.

va_pentagon_boulder.blurb: A large, tall boulder in Guest River Gorge in Southwest Virginia, sitting across from the Casablanca boulder in the Mile Two bouldering zone. Roughly eleven problems cover steep walls, vertical faces and a bit of slab, with some sections well featured and others fairly blank. The grades start around V1, include a handful in the V3 to V5 range, and top out with a couple of hard V7 lines, so it suits stronger boulderers more than beginners. One line sits on the riverside face of the boulder.

va_roadside_boulder_2.blurb: A roughly 11-foot boulder at Grayson Highlands State Park, in the Boneyard zone beside the Left Boneyard. It is the first boulder you meet on the short walk toward the A.V.P. area and the Left Boneyard, which makes it a handy landmark as well as a place to climb. About eleven problems run from an easy V0 or V1 warm-up seam through a cluster of V3 and V4 lines to a couple of V5 problems. Pads are the only protection. A small stream can run in front of it in wet seasons.

va_towers.blurb: A small sport crag in Breaks Interstate Park in far Southwest Virginia, on the level beneath the Towers overlook and part of the wider Towers and Lodges climbing zone. About eleven routes, almost all of them bolted with a single trad line, spread from 5.8 up to a handful of 5.11s, with the middle of the range around 5.10. The crag is sunny, and some routes stay damp for about a day after rain. Most of the lines are in the moderate to hard range, so it works best for climbers comfortable leading 5.9 and above.

va_lower_ridge_trail_slabs.blurb: A quieter, lower-angle corner of Old Rag in Shenandoah National Park, tucked beside the Ridge Trail on the way up the mountain. Almost all of the roughly eleven routes are trad lines on granite slabs split by cracks, ranging from easy 5.3 climbs to a few at 5.10. Several are long, with some two-pitch lines, so a 60 m rope is useful. The slabs are among the gentlest climbing on Old Rag, which makes them a reasonable choice for newer trad leaders. Belays from the top and a hike or rappel back down are the norm.
